The project starts from a literal geometric reading of Minkowski spacetime and asks how far the known structure of physics can be recovered by following the geometry, projection, motion, coiling, braiding, and interaction rules before importing additional interpretive machinery.\\n\\nThe images below are not decorative. They are the fastest way into the construction. They show the recurring picture that runs through the SAT record: a trajectory through four-dimensional geometry, its intersection/readout on a time surface, increasing structural complexity through coiling and braiding, and the extension of the same grammar from particle-scale structures to interaction and cosmology.\\n\\n## Read the theory\\n\\n<table>\\n<tr>\\n<td width=\\\"25%\\\" valign=\\\"top\\\"><strong>Start with the idea</strong><br><a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/THE%20FUNDAMENTAL%20INTUITIONS%20%E2%80%94%20EXTENDED.pdf\\\">The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended</a><br><small>Foundational conceptual statement.</small></td>\\n<td width=\\\"25%\\\" valign=\\\"top\\\"><strong>Formal SAT presentation</strong><br><a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/FULL_THEORY.pdf\\\">FULL_THEORY.pdf</a><br><small>Compact mathematical presentation; awaiting independent vetting.</small></td>\\n<td width=\\\"25%\\\" valign=\\\"top\\\"><strong>Trace the derivations</strong><br><a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/..%5B%F0%9F%8E%9B%EF%B8%8F_NATHAN_DASH%5D/..Derivation_Index.md\\\">Derivation / provenance index</a><br><small>Map from major claims to source derivation attempts.</small></td>\\n<td width=\\\"25%\\\" valign=\\\"top\\\"><strong>Current H(s)H</strong><br><a href=\\\"synthesis/CURRENT_SYNTHESIS.md\\\">Current synthesis</a><br><small>Living reconstruction of the finite-core worldtube program.</small></td>\\n</tr>\\n</table>\\n\\n> **Read the pictures first if you want the fastest conceptual route.** The history, source record, formal work, current status, and growing document library are linked around and beneath them.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. One geometric construction, many familiar descriptions\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/01_unified_geometric_vision.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Unified geometric vision: QCD, relativity and string-like descriptions arising from one filament/time-surface geometry\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSAT's organizing move is not to invent a separate geometric story for every physical sector. It asks whether familiar descriptions can be understood as different projections, interaction regimes, or effective descriptions of one underlying geometric construction. The labels in historical figures should be read as **SAT mappings and research claims**, not as a substitute for the standard theories themselves.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. Particle differences as differences of geometry\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/02_particle_spectrum_geometry.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Spectrum of particles from a spectrum of geometry\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nA recurring SAT idea is that the apparent catalog of particle types may be reorganized as a catalog of trajectory geometries: simple traveling excitation, persistent coiling, and increasingly interdependent or braided structures. The current H(s)H program is working to replace the simplified centerline picture with a finite-core worldtube treatment while preserving the same geometric dependency structure.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. The basic readout: trajectory and time-surface intersection\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/03_helix_time_plane_intersection.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Helical trajectory intersecting a time surface\\\" width=\\\"78%\\\"></a>\\n\\nThe basic visual grammar is a higher-dimensional trajectory intersecting a lower-dimensional time slice or readout surface. The intersection can move, rotate, close, open, or change shape even when the underlying trajectory remains continuous.\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/04_theta4_tangent_time_normal.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Worldline tangent, time-field normal, and theta angle\\\" width=\\\"78%\\\"></a>\\n\\nHistorically SAT used an angular measure, usually written **θ₄**, to track the orientation of the trajectory relative to the time direction/surface normal. The notation and exact formal role have evolved; the geometric relationship is the durable part of the picture.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. Not just a straight helix: recursion and carrier geometry\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/05_recursive_helix_curved_carrier.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Recursive helix following a curved carrier\\\" width=\\\"76%\\\"></a>\\n\\nThe model is not simply \\\"everything is a helix.\\\" A local coil may itself propagate along a curved carrier, and that carrier may participate in still larger-scale structure. The present H(s)H work is focused on making this recursive, finite-core geometry explicit rather than leaving it compressed into a worldline skeleton.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 5. Interaction as geometric braiding\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/06_qcd_geometric_braiding.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"QCD analogy represented by geometric braiding\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSAT's braid-centered interaction picture treats multi-filament organization as a geometric relation rather than merely adding a new label to otherwise independent particles. In the historical worldline model this was represented by interweaving centerlines; H(s)H asks what the corresponding finite-core worldtube mechanics actually are: **bundle geometry + finite extent + intersection/readout + deformation**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 6. A worldline can generate an evolving family of observed patterns\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/08_worldline_time_slice_evolution.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Worldline propagation through successive time slices producing evolving geometric patterns\\\" width=\\\"76%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSuccessive slices through one continuous construction need not look alike. SAT repeatedly uses this fact to distinguish the full trajectory from the lower-dimensional pattern available at any one slice. The same distinction is central to the move from worldline to worldtube.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 7. The construction is intended to close at cosmological scale\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/09_geometric_cosmology_expansion.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"SAT geometric cosmology and expansion as resolution\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSAT was developed as a whole-physics translation program rather than a particle model alone. Its historical materials therefore extend the same geometric vocabulary into gravitation, large-scale structure, expansion, fluids, and cosmology. Some specific equations and historical mechanisms have since been revised or retired; the broad structural ambition remains part of H(s)H.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 8. Historical continuity is part of the record\\n\\nThe public H(s)H repository is not the primary historical archive. The larger [SAT Theory Archive 2023–25](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25) preserves the developmental record. One geometric construction, many familiar descriptions\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/01_unified_geometric_vision.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Unified geometric vision: QCD, relativity and string-like descriptions arising from one filament/time-surface geometry\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSAT's organizing move is not to invent a separate geometric story for every physical sector. Particle differences as differences of geometry\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/02_particle_spectrum_geometry.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Spectrum of particles from a spectrum of geometry\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nA recurring SAT idea is that the apparent catalog of particle types may be reorganized as a catalog of trajectory geometries: simple traveling excitation, persistent coiling, and increasingly interdependent or braided structures. The current H(s)H program is working to replace the simplified centerline picture with a finite-core worldtube treatment while preserving the same geometric dependency structure.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. The basic readout: trajectory and time-surface intersection\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/03_helix_time_plane_intersection.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Helical trajectory intersecting a time surface\\\" width=\\\"78%\\\"></a>\\n\\nThe basic visual grammar is a higher-dimensional trajectory intersecting a lower-dimensional time slice or readout surface. The intersection can move, rotate, close, open, or change shape even when the underlying trajectory remains continuous.\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/04_theta4_tangent_time_normal.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Worldline tangent, time-field normal, and theta angle\\\" width=\\\"78%\\\"></a>\\n\\nHistorically SAT used an angular measure, usually written **θ₄**, to track the orientation of the trajectory relative to the time direction/surface normal. The notation and exact formal role have evolved; the geometric relationship is the durable part of the picture.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. Not just a straight helix: recursion and carrier geometry\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/05_recursive_helix_curved_carrier.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Recursive helix following a curved carrier\\\" width=\\\"76%\\\"></a>\\n\\nThe model is not simply \\\"everything is a helix.\\\" A local coil may itself propagate along a curved carrier, and that carrier may participate in still larger-scale structure. The present H(s)H work is focused on making this recursive, finite-core geometry explicit rather than leaving it compressed into a worldline skeleton.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 5. Interaction as geometric braiding\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/06_qcd_geometric_braiding.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"QCD analogy represented by geometric braiding\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSAT's braid-centered interaction picture treats multi-filament organization as a geometric relation rather than merely adding a new label to otherwise independent particles. In the historical worldline model this was represented by interweaving centerlines; H(s)H asks what the corresponding finite-core worldtube mechanics actually are: **bundle geometry + finite extent + intersection/readout + deformation**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 6. A worldline can generate an evolving family of observed patterns\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/08_worldline_time_slice_evolution.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Worldline propagation through successive time slices producing evolving geometric patterns\\\" width=\\\"76%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSuccessive slices through one continuous construction need not look alike. Source preservation\\n+\\n+**Never overwrite original source artifacts in place as part of extraction, conversion, OCR, image extraction, normalization, indexing, or analysis.**\\n+\\n+Derived products must go to a declared output namespace and, where practical, record:\\n+- source repo/path;\\n+- source blob/content hash;\\n+- extraction/conversion tool version;\\n+- run ID;\\n+- generated artifact hash.\\n+\\n+Examples:\\n+- PDF/image extraction -> dedicated extraction/output tree;\\n+- conversation normalization -> generated Viewer/index tree, not the raw conversation file;\\n+- OCR/text extraction -> derived text file alongside provenance metadata, not replacement of the original binary.\\n+\\n+A source may be deliberately edited only by a workflow whose explicit purpose is to edit that source, with the semantic-write protections below.\\n+\\n+## Quarantine and sandbox\\n+\\n+- Ordinary scripts must not descend into or read quarantine-controlled trees unless the workflow is explicitly authorized for that quarantine.\\n+- Path pruning must occur **before file open/hash/index/sample operations**, not merely before publishing results.\\n+- Quarantine-derived material must not leak into ordinary manifests, search indexes, logs, samples, filenames, or error reports beyond authorized minimal routing metadata.\\n+- Direct theory construction/development remains sandbox-routed; infrastructure scripts must preserve sandbox/public/private distinctions rather than flatten them.\\n+\\n+## Write classes\\n+\\n+### A. Read-only / audit\\n+Safest class. May inventory/hash/read permitted sources but makes no repo changes.\\n+\\n+Requirements:\\n+- exact source refs recorded;\\n+- quarantine pruning before descent;\\n+- outputs, if retained, are written separately as derived artifacts.\\n+\\n+### B. Derived/generated output\\n+Examples: extracted images/text, manifests, Viewer catalogs, indexes, samples, generated reports.\\n+\\n+Requirements:\\n+- deterministic/rebuildable when feasible;\\n+- write only inside declared generated/output paths;\\n+- do not overwrite source artifacts;\\n+- compare generated source coverage against current inputs before declaring success;\\n+- publish from a fresh base;\\n+- safe to regenerate rather than hand-merge when appropriate.\\n+\\n+### C. Append-only operational logs/handoffs\\n+Requirements:\\n+- re-fetch immediately before append;\\n+- preserve existing entries exactly;\\n+- if append cannot be made atomically or against current state, abort/retry rather than replace from a stale copy.\\n+\\n+### D. Shared semantic state\\n+Examples: central checkpoints, controlling status files, manually curated synthesis/control documents.\\n+\\n+Requirements:\\n+- re-fetch immediately before write;\\n+- use current blob SHA / compare-and-swap semantics where available;\\n+- if target changed since read, abort or reconcile explicitly;\\n+- never silently whole-file replace from stale cached content;\\n+- minimize independent writers;\\n+- prefer worker-local state + handoff + aggregation over many writers editing one central file.\\n+\\n+### E. Destructive/renaming/migration jobs\\n+Examples: delete, move, mass rename, directory restructuring, source rewriting.\\n+\\n+Requirements:\\n+- dry-run/default preview unless the operation is trivial and fully deterministic;\\n+- pre-run manifest of affected paths and hashes;\\n+- explicit source/destination collision handling;\\n+- no overwrite-on-collision unless the workflow specifically proves identity and records the action;\\n+- reversible mapping or backup/provenance sufficient to reconstruct prior location/content;\\n+- post-run integrity check.\\n+\\n+## GitHub Contents API writes\\n+\\n+For replacement updates, use the current blob SHA. This provides compare-and-swap behavior: stale writes should fail rather than silently clobber a newer version.\\n+\\n+Required pattern:\\n+1. fetch current target + SHA;\\n+2. compute/reconcile update;\\n+3. update with that SHA;\\n+4. on stale-SHA failure, re-fetch and retry/reconcile; do not bypass the guard.\\n+\\n+## Git checkout / commit / push writes\\n+\\n+Before publishing:\\n+1. fetch current target branch;\\n+2. rebase/reset/merge onto current branch as appropriate;\\n+3. rerun any validation whose assumptions could have changed;\\n+4. push without force;\\n+5. if rejected, fetch again and retry non-destructively or stop for reconciliation.\\n+\\n+**Never force-push automated generated or semantic project updates to `main`.**\\n+\\n+One-shot stage -> run -> cleanup GitHub Actions are allowed when their workflow is narrow, validated, and uses this fresh-base publish pattern.\\n+\\n+## Concurrency\\n+\\n+Use repository/workflow concurrency controls when two runs of the same job could overlap.\\n+\\n+Concurrency controls are a convenience, not the primary integrity mechanism: scripts must still tolerate another actor changing the repository while they run.\\n+\\n+For long-running jobs:\\n+- snapshot exact input commits at start;\\n+- treat output as a product of those snapshots;\\n+- before publishing semantic changes, reconcile against current target state;\\n+- generated outputs may either publish snapshot-stamped results or rerun against newer input, but must not pretend stale input was current.\\n+\\n+## Cross-repo jobs\\n+\\n+A job reading multiple repositories must treat each repository as an independent versioned input.\\n+\\n+Record the commit SHA for every repo. Do not use vague labels such as `latest` in retained run manifests.\\n+\\n+If a combined output contains metadata/content from a private repository, default its destination to a private repository. Publication to a public repo requires an explicit safe-publication decision; do not infer one from the fact that other inputs were public.\\n+\\n+## Image / OCR / extraction jobs\\n+\\n+Because rename/move into final destination;\\n+- if final destination already exists with the same source/tool identity, verify/reuse rather than blindly overwrite;\\n+- if it differs, preserve both or route to reconciliation.\\n+\\n+## Temporary files\\n+\\n+Temporary/state files must be either:\\n+- outside repository trees; or\\n+- inside a clearly designated ignored/generated temp namespace.\\n+\\n+Do not leave generic names such as `output.json`, `temp.txt`, or `result.csv` at shared roots where concurrent jobs can overwrite one another.\\n+\\n+## Validation / post-run checks\\n+\\n+A script that succeeded from a fresh base.\\n+\\n+Unexpected writes outside declared scope are a failure condition.\\n+\\n+## Run manifest / auditability\\n+\\n+For substantial recurring or cross-repo jobs, prefer silent data loss.\\n+\\n+## Worker / automation obligations\\n+\\n+- Workers may propose improvements, but Sable owns cross-lane workflow redesign and project-wide execution-safety policy unless Existing scripts are grandfathered only temporarily; upgrade them when touched or when they become active collision risks.\\n+- Repeated manual scripts should be promoted toward repo-native, or\\n- inside a clearly designated ignored/generated temp namespace.\\n\\nDo not leave generic names such as `output.json`, `temp.txt`, or `result.csv` at shared roots where concurrent jobs can overwrite one another.\\n\\n## Validation / post-run checks\\n\\nA script that writes should perform checks appropriate to its job, such as:\\n- expected outputs exist and are nonempty;\\n- JSON/YAML/CSV syntax validates;\\n- source count/coverage is plausible;\\n- output source IDs/hashes map back to actual inputs;\\n- no source files changed unexpectedly;\\n- quarantine exclusions remain absent;\\n- git diff contains only declared write scope;\\n- commit/push succeeded from a fresh base.\\n\\nUnexpected writes outside declared scope are a failure condition.\\n\\n## Run manifest / auditability\\n\\nFor substantial recurring or cross-repo jobs, prefer a compact machine-readable run record containing:\\n- run ID;\\n- start/end time;\\n- tool version;\\n- input repo SHAs;\\n- declared read/write scope;\\n- output hashes/counts;\\n- exclusions/quarantine-root counts without leaking quarantined content;\\n- success/failure status;\\n- published commit SHA(s).\\n\\nDo not record credentials/tokens.\\n\\n## Failure behavior\\n\\nOn ambiguity, collision, stale target, unknown source identity, or unexpected diff:\\n\\n**STOP / RETRY / ROUTE — never guess and overwrite.**\\n\\nA failed run is preferable to silent data loss.\\n\\n## Worker / automation obligations\\n\\n- Workers may propose improvements, but Sable owns cross-lane workflow redesign and project-wide execution-safety policy unless Nathan says otherwise.\\n- Infrastructure QA should audit scripts/workflows for compliance opportunistically and after incidents.\\n- Newly written scripts should comply from first use.\\n- Existing scripts are grandfathered only temporarily;
